title: Min stack

invariants.inv-min-tracks: The min-stack's top always equals the minimum of every value currently in the main stack.

why_it_exists.problem: While a standard stack provides O(1) access to the top element, querying a global property like the minimum value requires an O(n) linear scan.
why_it_exists.better_idea: Leverage the immutable historical nature of LIFO structures. Capture a snapshot of the minimum value at the exact moment an element is pushed, storing it in a parallel auxiliary stack.
why_it_exists.naive_solution: Scanning the entire stack from top to bottom every time you need the minimum value, taking O(n) time.

mental_model.intuition: Keep a shadow stack running next to the main stack, where every element represents the absolute minimum value seen up to that depth.
mental_model.description: The optimal solution uses an auxiliary 'min-stack'. When pushing a value x, compare it to the current minimum (the top of the min-stack), and push the lesser of the two onto the min-stack. When popping, both stacks pop simultaneously. This guarantees the top of the min-stack always holds the global minimum of the current elements in O(1) time.
mental_model.repeated_decision: When pushing x, what is smaller: x, or the current minimum at the top of the min-stack?

engineering_examples.title: Streaming min/max ('min-queue')
engineering_examples.problem: Reporting the minimum of a stream that supports both ends in O(1)
engineering_examples.why_this_algorithm: Two min-stacks compose into a FIFO queue that returns its minimum in amortized O(1) — the classic 'min-queue' used inside sliding-window and streaming-analytics code. The stack is the reusable building block.

failure_signals: Linearly scanning the stack on every getMin request

pattern.name: Parallel State Tracking
recognition_cues: Design a stack that supports getMin/getMax in O(1)
Need to query global state of a LIFO structure instantly

common_mistakes.title: Forgetting to sync pops
common_mistakes.explanation: If you only push to the min-stack when a new minimum is found, you must be extremely careful during popping to only pop the min-stack if the popped value equals the current minimum. Using a parallel 1:1 stack avoids this sync issue entirely.

common_mistakes.title: Differential encoding underflow/overflow
common_mistakes.explanation: An O(1) space optimization exists using mathematical differential encoding, but it risks integer overflow (`2*x - min_val`). Production systems must use 64-bit bounds checking.

recall_questions.q: How does the parallel min-stack achieve O(1) time complexity for getMin()?
recall_questions.answer: It captures and stores a snapshot of the global minimum at every specific stack depth, effectively memorizing the answer for any given state.

recall_questions.q: Why is state snapshotting possible in a stack but harder in a dynamic array?
recall_questions.answer: A stack strictly mutates at a single boundary (the top). Elements below the top are immutable as long as the stack height exceeds their depth.

recall_questions.q: What is the space complexity of the standard parallel min-stack approach?
recall_questions.answer: O(n) auxiliary space to store the shadow stack of minimums.

oa_questions.question: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time.
oa_questions.answer: Use a main stack for values and an auxiliary stack that pushes `min(x, current_min)`. Both pop simultaneously.

oa_questions.question: Optimize Min Stack to use O(1) extra space.
oa_questions.answer: Use differential encoding. Store an anomaly value `2*x - min_val` when a new minimum is found. Upon popping an anomaly, decode it to restore the previous minimum. Decode step: if a popped value is < current min, it was an encoded flag — recover the previous min as `2*min - popped`; the real data value equals the old min.

practice.title: Max Stack
practice.why: The same concept applied to finding the maximum, with an added twist for removing the maximum.

explanation:
Min Stack perfectly highlights how leveraging invariants can circumvent seemingly mandatory linear scans. Because the physical structure of a stack guarantees that historical elements cannot be removed out of order, the statistical properties of that history (such as the minimum) are statically locked until popped.

While the O(n) space double-stack method is completely standard, being able to articulate the O(1) mathematical differential encoding (storing a transformed value to flag a state change) demonstrates an elite understanding of state management and boundary risks (overflow).

hook.scenario: You have a stack of numbers, and you constantly need to know the smallest one. Scanning the whole stack takes too long.
hook.question: How can we know the minimum instantly, even as numbers are added and removed?

key_points.title: Invariant
key_points.detail: The minimum state is perfectly synchronized with the main stack's lifecycle.

key_points.title: Complexity
key_points.detail: O(1) time for push, pop, and getMin.

key_points.title: Gotcha
key_points.detail: When popping, ensure the parallel minimum state is also popped to remain synchronized.
